    StartersFerdinand's farmyard egg sandwichesEgg mayo with chives on soft white bread, cut in trianglesHow to make it6 eggs3 tbsp mayonnaise1 bunch chiveswhite pepper, to taste8 slices of soft white bread1/4 iceberg lettuceBoil the eggs hard, then cool in cold water and peel.Mash the eggs with the mayonnaise, chopped chives and white pepper.Spread on the bread with shredded lettuce, close up and cut into triangles.Sheepdog trial cheesePecorino, sheep's feta and ricotta with fresh figs and honeyHow to make it150g pecorino150g sheep's feta200g fresh ricotta4 figs2 tbsp honey1 packet crackersTake the cheeses out of the fridge an hour ahead so they lose the chill.Halve the figs, then arrange the pecorino, sheep's feta and fresh ricotta on a board with the figs, drizzle over the honey and put the crackers alongside.Ferdinand's crudités and green goddessFerdinand the duck, sneaking round the vegie patchHow to make itAs written, serves 4Crisp baby carrots, radish, cucumber, snow peas and cherry tomatoes with a bright green goddess dip of herbs, sour cream and lemon.Blitz 150g sour cream, 80g mayonnaise, a handful each of parsley, basil and chives, 1 spring onion, the juice of half a lemon and salt until smooth and green.Chill 30 minutes.Trim 1 bunch baby carrots and 1 bunch radishes, cut 1 Lebanese cucumber into sticks and top 150g snow peas.Arrange around the dip with 250g cherry tomatoes.Beetroot relish and cheddar sconesMrs Hoggett's baking, Ferdinand at the window.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsShepherd's pieBeef mince in tomato gravy under baked mashed potatoHow to make it750g beef mince1 brown onion2 carrots2 tbsp tomato paste2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce250ml beef stock1kg potatoes60g buttersalt and pepper, to tasteDice the onion and carrots. Peel the potatoes and cut into chunks.Brown the mince hard in a large pan, then add the onion and carrot and cook a few minutes.Stir in the tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce and stock and simmer until thick, then season with salt and pepper.Boil the potatoes until soft, drain and mash with the butter.Spoon the mince into a baking dish, top with mash and fork the surface. Bake at 200°C until golden.Farmhouse leek, mushroom and cheddar pieNo pigs or ducks were harmed in this pieHow to make itAs written, serves 4Leek, mushroom and potato in a creamy cheddar and thyme sauce under a golden puff pastry lid, with buttered peas on the side.Boil 500g diced potato for 8 minutes and drain.Cook 2 sliced leeks and 300g sliced mushrooms in 40g butter for 10 minutes.Stir in 2 tbsp flour, then 400ml milk and simmer 3 minutes.Add 150g grated cheddar, thyme, the potato, salt and pepper.Pour into a pie dish, cover with 2 sheets puff pastry, brush with egg and bake at 200°C for 30 minutes.Serve with 400g buttered peas.SweetsHoggett farm apple crumbleStewed cinnamon apples under a butter crumble, with custardHow to make it6 apples60g caster sugar1 tsp cinnamon100g butter100g plain flour60g rolled oats80g brown sugar600ml custardPeel, core and slice the apples.Stew the apples with the caster sugar and cinnamon until just soft, then tip into a baking dish.Rub the cold butter into the flour, then stir in the oats and brown sugar. Scatter over the apples.Bake at 180°C until golden and bubbling. Heat the custard and serve alongside.DrinksHoggett farm vanilla malted shakeVanilla ice cream and malt blended thick, topped with whipped creamHow to make it600ml full cream milk6 scoops of vanilla ice cream4 tbsp malted milk powder, for the shake1 tbsp honey150ml thickened cream2 tsp malted milk powder, for dustingChill four tall glasses. Whip the cream to soft peaks.Blend the milk, ice cream, the malted milk powder for the shake and the honey until thick and frothy.Pour into the glasses, spoon the cream on top and dust with the extra malted milk powder.Warm spiced milk with honeyThat'll do, pig. That'll do.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
